comparator.name: Economics and Business Economics (Economie en Bedrijfseconomie)
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–2027 Economics track totals 180 EC: ten compulsory 6 EC courses in each of Years 1 and 2, 30 EC open study, three compulsory 6 EC final-year subjects and a 12 EC Economics thesis. Economics is the first-listed broad track in the official schedule, selected neutrally before UCR construction; Accounting, Finance and Marketing belong to the separate Business Economics track and are not mixed into this comparator. English teaching has Dutch tutorial, expression and exam-answer options in Years 1–2; Year 3 is English. BSA normally requires 42 first-year EC and a pass in QRM I. The English diagnostic or completed refresher gates the Academic Skills grade. Zero-credit SAM provides mentor meetings each period, not added EC. The second-year Research Paper is a three-student project with data/model-based inquiry, paper, referee report and presentations; QRM I/II and Academic Skills are recommended background. Thesis entry at application requires 120 EC including QRM II, the entire first year, and at most two outstanding Year-2 courses. It is individual literature-review or empirical/theoretical economic research with thesis and video presentation; apply early October for periods 2–3 or late February for periods 5–6. These relative deadlines are not imposed as dated future-cohort deadlines. Open study normally requires 90 EC, at most 6 EC level 100, at least 12 EC level 300, no compulsory overlap and prior examination-board approval except SBE faculty, university or Education minors. Business Administration and Economics university minors are prohibited for EBE. Course manuals may require attendance; the Ethics tutorials and two online meetings are compulsory. Honours is additional. The main annual chart shows thesis12EC, but the specialisation subtable incorrectly prints6EC; the exact annual thesis catalogue independently confirms12EC. Retain12EC, not an invented extra unit or guessed two-part6EC allocation. Hidden duplicate text in the main chart is not an additional Macroeconomics course.

questionsApplications.label: How do economic policies affect labour markets, inequality and broad prosperity?
How can banks manage risk and remain financially stable?
How do consumers respond to marketing and firm decisions?
Can energy choices such as nuclear power address climate change sustainably?

alternatives.concept: Economic theory and empirical methods organise the study of public policy, welfare, financial decisions and sustainable prosperity. Microeconomics, international macroeconomics, public economics, behavioral economics and applied econometrics provide the substantive economic response. Climate science, ethics, institutional governance and firm-level decisions make specific complements; they do not replace VU’s specialist development, regional/transport, human-capital and economic-policy courses or thesis.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Four courses/30EC differ on each side. Programming, Consumer Product Design, Negotiation and Digital Strategy replace Public Economics, Climate Change, Ethics and Money/Banking. The consumer option prioritises customer investigation and business strategy; the primary option prioritises public welfare, sustainability and financial decisions. Programming enables its digital/data implementation; no arbitrary substitutions are used.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Retain two qualified responses: an economics/public-policy programme and a distinct consumer/marketing application. The Finance candidate has genuine financial-decision and business-law contributions, but one7.5ECbanking/finance course and accounting, generic discrete/linear mathematics and governance do not implement its advertised specialised investment/financial-stability progression. No distinct full finance alternative is established. Accounting lacks an advanced accounting/information-systems sequence. Nuclear energy is a single illustrative climate-policy question, not a stable independent academic direction; its broader sustainability issue belongs to the primary option. No third alternative is manufactured.

notes.text: The UCR options provide economic theory, quantitative and applied econometric methods, and either public-policy or consumer/business applications. They do not reproduce VU’s dedicated development, spatial/transport, human-capital and economic-policy sequence, specialist business-economics routes or compulsory Economics thesis. Accounting concerns financial statements; general mathematics and governance do not establish a specialist Finance programme. No degree equivalence or automatic master’s eligibility is implied.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Economics and Business Economics studies decisions by people, firms and governments through economic theory, quantitative methods and research. After common first-year study, students choose Economics or Business Economics, with Accounting, Finance and Marketing specialisations in the latter.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Two qualified UCR alternatives retain substantial economic theory and empirical methods. One emphasises public welfare, sustainability and financial decisions; the other emphasises consumer evidence, marketing and digital business. Their specific complementary courses do not replace the full specialist VU sequence or compulsory thesis.

curriculum.limitation: The selected Economics pathway contains 180 EC, including 30 EC open study and a 12 EC individual thesis. Thesis entry requires 120 EC including QRM II, all first-year courses and at most two remaining second-year courses. The English diagnostic or refresher gates Academic Skills; zero-credit SAM mentoring is separate. The minor has level, approval and nonoverlap conditions; Economics and Business Administration university minors are prohibited.
